stem: female presents with a bulge in the right groin, located below the inguinal ligament. For the past day, she has not passed flatus. Previously, the bulge would come and go, but now, she is unable to reduce it back manually and no skin change or discoloration ?
srcNote: The check mark is reproduced from the source; no separate answer key is provided.
expl: A bulge below the inguinal ligament in a woman = femoral hernia. Irreducible with no flatus but no skin change/discolouration = incarcerated (with obstruction), not yet strangulated.

why.B: Strangulation would show skin changes, severe tenderness and systemic upset.
why.C: Inguinal hernias lie above the ligament.
why.D: Wrong site, and no strangulation signs.

stem: A 50-year-old man has a groin bulge that enlarges on standing or coughing. What is the diagnosis?
ansText: Inguinal hernia — a reducible groin bulge with a cough impulse that enlarges with raised intra-abdominal pressure.

stem: A 60-year-old male with a history of cirrhosis and ascites presents with a hernia, it appears to be a hernia with fat content , what is the management?

opts.t: Manage the ascites and hernia repair

srcNote: The check mark is reproduced from the source; no separate answer key is provided.
expl: Ascites raises intra-abdominal pressure and causes recurrence, leaks and infection after repair → optimise (control) the ascites first, then repair the hernia (repair is not contraindicated).

why.B: Repair is not contraindicated — it is done after optimisation.

stem: A 2 months old girl was brought to the clinic with a history of left groin swelling that increases while crying and decreases during sleep. On physical examination, there is a reducible left inguinal swelling. Which ONEofthe following is the appropriate management?
expl: Inguinal hernias in infants don't resolve and have a high risk of incarceration → herniotomy as early as possible (elective, soon after diagnosis).

stem: A 34-year-old man who underwent open repair of right inguinal hernia 3 years ago presented with right groin swelling for 3 months associated with dragging pain. Physical examination revealed reducible swelling in the right groin with positive cough impulse, reaching the neck of scrotum. Which of the following is the appropriate repair?
srcNote: (Abdominal wall and herniae) The sources differ on whether the laparoscopic repair uses mesh. Both original answer versions are retained. Other source key (Final 439 F Q45): Answer: A. In that version: A. Laparoscopic inguinal hernia without mesh.
expl: Recurrence after an open anterior repair → use the other approach — laparoscopic (posterior) mesh repair, through virgin tissue planes.

why.B: Re-operating through scarred anterior planes is harder and riskier.
why.D: Darning is an old tissue repair.

stem: A 2 year old boy has a right inguinal hernia came with his parents because it became irreducible for the last 6 hours with no skin changes. Which one of the following is the diagnosis?
srcNote: (Abdominal wall and herniae)
expl: A known hernia that becomes irreducible for 6 hours without skin changes = incarcerated inguinal hernia.

why.A: A hydrocele isn't "irreducible hernia" and transilluminates.
why.C: Lipoma isn't a hernia that became irreducible.
why.D: Strangulation would show skin changes, tenderness, systemic signs.

stem: A 5-year-old girl is referred your clinic with an umbilical swelling since birth. On physical examination the swelling is easily reducible, and a one-centimeter defect is felt at the umbilicus. What is the best advice to her parents?
srcNote: (Abdominal wall and herniae)
expl: Most umbilical hernias close by age 4–5; a persisting defect in a 5-year-old is unlikely to close → surgical repair.

why.B: She is beyond the age of spontaneous closure.
why.D: No reason to wait to puberty.

stem: patient presented with strangulated hernia. Where do you expect to find it
srcNote: Only three options are supplied in the source.
expl: A hernia obstructs the bowel from outside the wall → extramural (extrinsic) cause.

stem: You saw two patient with inguinal hernia what is the structure to diffrentiate between direct and indirect hernia??
srcNote: (Abdominal wall and herniae) One or more options are blank in the source.
expl: The inferior epigastric vessels: indirect hernias are lateral, direct hernias medial.

why.A: The superior epigastric vessels are higher in the rectus sheath.

stem: a 32 years old male presented with lift groin swelling not descending to the scrotum what is the most likely cause ?
srcNote: ? (Abdominal wall and herniae) The original source marks its answer as uncertain; the key is preserved without correction.
expl: Keyed: indirect hernia — the commonest groin hernia at all ages, even when not yet in the scrotum (a direct hernia rarely enters the scrotum, so a non-scrotal swelling could be either).

why.B: Femoral is below the ligament and in women.
why.C: Direct is possible, but indirect remains commonest.
why.D: Obturator hernias are rare and not visible in the groin.

stem: What defect can cause an indirect inguinal hernia in children?
srcNote: Options C and D contain only their labels in the source.
expl: Paediatric indirect hernias come from a patent processus vaginalis (congenital).

why.B: Hesselbach's weakness = direct hernia in adults.

stem: 25-year-Old healthy man with no previous history of abdominal surgery. presented to the emergency department complaining of severe colicky abdominal pain for 6 hours associated with frequent vomiting, and abdominal distension. Physical examination revealed diffuse abdominal distention with exaggerated bowel sounds. Which of the following Is the most appropriate initial step in management?
expl: SBO in a virgin abdomen → examine the hernia orifices (groins) first.

why.C: Laparotomy comes after finding the cause.

stem: Which of the following nerves can be injured during surgery for inguinal hernia repair?

opts.t: Ilioinguinal nerve, iliohypogastric nerve, genitofemoral nerve
Pudendal nerve, iliohypogastric nerve, popliteal nerve
Ilioinguinal nerve, pudendal nerve, iliohypogastric nerve
Ilioinguinal nerve, femoral nerve, genitofemoral nerve

srcNote: (surgical complications)
expl: Inguinal hernia repair can injure the ilioinguinal, iliohypogastric and genitofemoral nerves (chronic groin pain/numbness).

why.B: Pudendal and popliteal aren't in the field.

stem: A 5 month old baby girl presents with umbilical swelling. On examination, it is easily reducible. What is the management of this case?

opts.t: Surgical repair after age of 1 year if not spontaneously resolved
Surgical repair between 4-5 years of age if not spontaneously resolved

srcNote: The source versions give different age ranges for repair; their wording is retained. Source note (Final 436 A Q22): Answer: D. In that version: D. Surgical repair between 3-4 years of age if not spontaneously resolved. Source note (Final 435 F Q11 (p. 144)): Ans: D (Abdominal wall and herniae). In the 6-month-old version: D. Reassure and follow up.
expl: Infantile umbilical hernias usually close spontaneously → observe; repair at 4–5 years if persisting (earlier if very large or symptomatic).

why.A: Follow-up is needed in case it persists.

stem: What is the most common hernia in 60 y.o Saudi male?
srcNote: (Abdominal wall and herniae)
expl: Keyed: indirect inguinal hernia is the commonest hernia at all ages, including older men (direct hernias increase with age but indirect stays commonest).

stem: What type of hernia protrudes through the superficial inguinal ring and has positive cough impulse?
srcNote: (Abdominal wall and herniae) Both direct and indirect has positive cough impulse and Both protrudes through the superficial inguinal ring even though indirect herniate through superficial and deep also making A more specific answer The original source supplies alternative answers and an explanation; both are retained as written.
expl: Both direct and indirect inguinal hernias can emerge through the superficial ring with a cough impulse (the indirect via the canal; the direct through the posterior wall then out of the superficial ring). The source accepted both.

why.C: Femoral hernias emerge through the femoral canal, below the ligament.
why.D: Ventral hernias are in the abdominal wall.

stem: What is the most common type of hernia in 55 y.o female?
srcNote: (Abdominal wall and herniae)
expl: Inguinal hernia is the commonest hernia in women too; femoral hernia is relatively more common in women than in men but is still less common than inguinal.

stem: A 3 month old had hernia and the father had a history of hernia treated by mesh and he wanted his child to be treated with a mesh also. What would you advice him?

opts.t: Mesh isn’t required as the child needs herniotomy only
Mesh is only for umbilical hernia

srcNote: (Abdominal wall and herniae) One or more options are blank in the source.
expl: Paediatric inguinal hernia is a patent processus vaginalis — herniotomy (high ligation of the sac) is curative; the posterior wall is normal, so no mesh is needed.

why.B: Not an absolute contraindication — just unnecessary.

stem: What comes with epigastric hernia
srcNote: (Abdominal wall and herniae) One or more options are blank in the source.
expl: Epigastric hernias (through the linea alba above the umbilicus) are usually small, often containing only preperitoneal fat, and can be painful out of proportion.

why.B: A scar would point to an incisional hernia.

stem: what are the abdominal wall layers in order from most superficial to deep?

opts.t: Skin, superficial fascia. Transverse, external oblique, internal oblique, transversalis Fascia, peritoneum
Skin, superficial fascia, external oblique, internal oblique, Transverse, transversalis Fascia, peritoneum

srcNote: Options C and D are incomplete in the source.
expl: Superficial → deep: skin → superficial fascia (Camper's, Scarpa's) → external oblique → internal oblique → transversus abdominis → transversalis fascia → extraperitoneal fat → peritoneum.

stem: A 4-year-old boy is noted to have swelling in his right groin. He has no other symptoms. Physical examination shows no swelling, and both testes are in the scrotum, but the right spermatic cord is thickened with a positive cough impulse. What is the diagnostic imaging modality of choice to confirm the diagnosis?
srcNote: (Common pediatric surgical problems)
expl: A thickened cord with a cough impulse in a boy = clinical inguinal hernia ("silk sign") — no imaging needed.

why.B: US only if the diagnosis is doubtful.

stem: A 6-year-old male presents with a left groin lump. On examination, cough impulse is positive and the lump is reducible and extends into the scrotum. The internal ring occlusion test is positive. What type of hernia does the patient have?
srcNote: (Abdominal wall and herniae)
expl: Reducible lump extending into the scrotum, controlled by occluding the deep ring = indirect inguinal hernia (via the deep ring); in a child it is almost always indirect.

why.A: Direct isn't controlled by deep-ring occlusion and rarely reaches the scrotum.
why.C: Spigelian is in the lateral abdominal wall.

stem: Which one of the following physical signs is most important to confirm your diagnosis of inguinal hernia?

opts.t: Swelling above and lateral to pubic rami

srcNote: (not sure) (Abdominal wall and herniae) The original source marks its answer as uncertain; the key is preserved without correction.
expl: An expansile cough impulse is the most important sign confirming a hernia.

why.B: The site helps classify, but not confirm.

stem: A 28-year-old man presented with a history of reducible right inguinal hernia for 2 years which became painful since 16 hours associated with progressive abdominal distention and vomiting. Physical examination revealed distended abdomen, exaggerated bowel sound, tender right inguinal swelling with red discoloration of the overlying skin. Blood pressure 110/65 mmHg Heart rate 85 /min Temperature 38.2 Respiratory rate 18/min. Test Result Normal value WBC 9.8 4-10.5 x 10 9 L. Erect abdominal X-ray: Multiple air-fluid levels. Which of the following is the most likely hernia complication?
srcNote: (Abdominal wall and hernia)
expl: A known reducible hernia that becomes painful with distension and vomiting (obstruction) and is now tense and tender → strangulated (the most advanced, surgical emergency).

why.B: Obstructed is possible, but painful tense hernia with systemic signs = strangulation (keyed).

stem: A 3 months old boy was seen in a pediatric surgery clinic and was diagnosed with right inguinal hernia. He was booked for elective herniotomy. Two weeks before his elective surgery he was presented to the pediatric emergency department with irritability and reluctant to feed. His mother noticed persistent right inguinal swelling for the last 3 hours. Which of the following is the best management option?

opts.t: Trial of hernia reduction under sedation and analgesia
Observation in emergency for spontaneous reduction

srcNote: (but be aware trial of hernia reduction is not an option if strangulated) (Common pediatric inguinoscrotal conditions tutorial)
expl: An incarcerated infant hernia without signs of strangulation → try reduction under sedation/analgesia (usually successful), then herniotomy after 24–48 h when oedema settles.

why.A: Emergency surgery if reduction fails or strangulation is suspected.

stem: Child presenting with inguinal hernia. What is the characteristic that differentiate it from emergency cases?
srcNote: (Abdominal wall and herniae) Only three options are supplied in the source.
expl: Reducibility separates an elective hernia from an emergency (incarcerated/strangulated).

why.A: Skin changes are a late sign.

stem: Child brought by his parents to a general practitioner complaining of inguinal hernia. What to do next?
srcNote: (Abdominal wall and herniae) Only three options are supplied in the source.
expl: A child with an inguinal hernia should be referred to a paediatric surgeon for herniotomy — it won't resolve and can incarcerate.

stem: A 2 month old child with bilateral hernia and hydrocele what is the best Management?

opts.t: Bilateral hernia repair and evacuation of the hydrocele.
Bilateral hernia repair and observe hydrocele.
Observe until two years of age.

srcNote: (not sure ) (Common pediatric surgical problems) The original source marks its answer as uncertain; the key is preserved without correction.
expl: Bilateral hernias with hydrocele (both from a patent processus vaginalis) → repair both hernias and deal with the hydrocele at the same operation.

why.B: The hydrocele is evacuated at the same time.

stem: Regarding inguinal hernia repair under local anesthesia, which of the following nerve is usually blocked?
srcNote: (Abdominal wall and herniae) , Blocks of the ilioinguinal and iliohypogastric nerves may reduce the incidence of this chronic pain. Blocking the genital branch of genitofemoral nerve completes the nerve block for inguinal hernia surgeries. All these three nerves can be easily blocked under http://www.apicareonline.com/ultrasound-guided-hernia-blocks/
expl: Local-anaesthetic inguinal hernia repair blocks the ilioinguinal, iliohypogastric and genital branch of the genitofemoral nerves; of the choices only the iliohypogastric is involved.

stem: Regarding the direct inguinal hernia:

opts.t: its medial to the inferior epigastric artery

expl: A direct hernia lies medial to the inferior epigastric artery, through Hesselbach's triangle.

why.C: Direct hernias are rare in women.
why.D: Right-sided predominance belongs to indirect hernias.

stem: which of the following is true regarding femoral hernia:

opts.t: Located just above and medial to the pubic tubercle

srcNote: , it’s common in female however, inguinal hernia is the commonest among all hernias
expl: Femoral hernias have the highest risk of complications (incarceration/strangulation) because of the narrow, rigid femoral ring. They lie below and lateral to the pubic tubercle and are more common in women than men, but inguinal hernias are still the commonest in women.

stem: all goes through aponeurosis except:
expl: Keyed: umbilical hernia — a congenital hernia through the umbilical ring (scar) rather than through an aponeurotic defect. Paraumbilical and epigastric hernias pass through the linea alba aponeurosis. (A femoral hernia passes through the femoral canal — the key chose umbilical.)

why.B: Through the linea alba next to the umbilicus.
why.C: Through the linea alba above the umbilicus.

stem: All true about Direct hernia except:
srcNote: Only three options are supplied in the source.
expl: A direct hernia pushes through the weak transversalis fascia of Hesselbach's triangle — not through the fascia iliaca. It doesn't enter through the deep ring (so doesn't truly traverse the canal), and makes up a large share of adult groin hernias.

why.C: True — it doesn't pass through the deep ring.

stem: Strangulation

opts.t: Is ischemia to the protruded organs

srcNote: Incomplete recall: only two statements are supplied in the source. Year not stated
expl: Strangulation = compromised blood supply → ischaemia of the hernia contents. It can be repaired laparoscopically in experienced hands.

stem: Patient presented with strangulated hernia part of the bowel was resected and primary anastomosis was done. Which of the following is the best treatment modality?
srcNote: a (Abdominal wall and herniae)
expl: The source had no key. After bowel resection the field is contaminated → repair with the patient's tissues (herniorrhaphy) rather than mesh (hernioplasty), to avoid infected mesh.

why.B: Mesh in a contaminated field risks infection.

stem: During laparotomy for an obstructed hernia, only part of the circumference of the bowel wall is found in the sac. What is it called?
srcNote: a (Abdominal wall and herniae) Only one option is supplied in this recalled question.
ansText: Richter's hernia — only part of the antimesenteric wall is trapped; it can strangulate and perforate without complete obstruction (commonly femoral).
